newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch-March 20.
newsitem.headline: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch-March 20.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors affecting Indian stock markets on Thursday morning:
NEWS OUTLOOK:
** India's biggest mutual fund, the Unit Trust of India is launching the country's first offshore 100 percent debt fund, the Economic Times daily reports.
The fund, to be domiciled in Mauritius, is aimed at overseas investors interested in participating in Indian debt and will be launched in a few months time, the paper says.
** India's rightwing Hindu Bharatiya Janata Party said on Wednesday it had agreed with an influential party of lower-caste Hindus to form a government in the northern state of Uttar Pradesh.
India's most populous state has been ruled directly by New Delhi after inconclusive local elections in September last year failed to produce a clear majority for any one political group.
** Market regulator, the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) on Wednesday set norms for "negotiated deals" or off-market transactions.

"It has been decided that with effect from June 1, 1997 all negotiated deals ... would compulsorily result in delivery of securities," the market watchdog said in a statement after a day-long meeting with officials of 22 exchanges.
"This would eliminate some of the possible malpractices," it said, without elaborating.
Presently, such negotiated deals are squared-up by market players, brokers said.
** SEBI said it did not decide on uniform settlements for all exchanges after some of them opposed the proposal at the meeting held on Wednesday.

** State-run Union Bank of India (UBI) announced a 50-basis-point cut in its prime lending rate, taking its rate for prime customers from 14.5 percent to 14 percent with effect from April 1, the Economic Times reports.

The 0.5 percentage point cut also brought down the maximum rate that could be charged by the bank to 18 percent from 18.5 percent. UBI was the first bank to respond to the finance minister's statement to cut lending rates, the paper says.
MARKETS:
** The Indian rupee opened at 35.8950/9050 on Thursday against the previous close of 35.8900/8950, dealers said.
* The opening rates reflected the weekend carrying cost for Thursday's spot transactions, dealers said.
** Shares at Indian exchanges took a sharp fall on Wednesday, as financial year-end considerations preyed on the minds of major players, dealers said.
** The benchmark Bombay Stock Exchange 30-share index tumbled 106.10 points, or 2.80 percent, to end at 3,689.07.
** The National Stock Exchange index dropped 1.16 percent, to 1,052.05.
** The Delhi share index lost 1.95 percent to 773.05.
** The Calcutta index shed 2.05 points to 453.69.
** The Madras share index eased 1.87 percent to 3,535.29.
